Present: Mr. Ravinder Malik (Ravi), Sr. Advocate
 with Mr. Garvit Mittal, Advocate
 and Mr. Ritender Rathee, Advocate
 for the petitioner.
 Mr. Vikrant Pamboo, Advocate
 for respondents No.1 to 5.
Harpreet Singh Brar J. (Oral)
1.

Prayer in this writ petition filed under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution of India, is for issuance of a writ in the nature of certiorari, for quashing the impugned enquiry report dated 15.02.2023 (Annexure P-23) submitted by respondent No.6 and the dismissal order dated 23.05.2023 (Annexure P-24) vide which the petitioner has been ordered to be dismissed from service.

Further a writ of mandamus has been sought, directing the respondents to reinstate the petitioner back in service and grant him full salary from the date of dismissal till reinstatement along with interest @ 18% per annum on arrears.
Another prayer has been made to direct respondent No.1 to hear and decide the appeal filed by the petitioner against the impugned dismissal order dated 23.05.2023 (Annexure P-24).

Learned counsel for the petitioner, inter alia, contends that the petitioner was falsely implicated in FIR No.109 dated 08.02.2022, registered under Sections 34/120-B/201/409/420/467/468/471 IPC and Section 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, only on the basis of the disclosure Kulwant Singh vs Chairman, Haryana Power Utilities And ... on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12134564/
1 statement made by co-accused, which has no evidentiary value in the eyes of law.

sentences.text: The petitioner was not named in the FIR (supra).
On 23.06.2022, the respondent/Nigam issued a charge- sheet to the petitioner which was served on 06.09.2022 through special messenger while the petitioner was in judicial custody.

Respondent No.5 was appointed as an Enquiry Officer, despite being 84 years of age and he was not authorized to be appointed as an Enquiry Officer in terms of the Government Instructions dated 15.03.2022, which prohibits the appointment of Enquiry Officer beyond the age of 70 years.
The petitioner made a detailed representations on 09.12.2022 and 01.03.2023 for changing the Enquiry Officer in view of the aforesaid Instructions.

The co-accused of the petitioner,
who were also charge- sheeted in the departmental proceedings have approached this Court by way of filing a petition i.e. CWP-28827-2022 whereas the petitioner has filed a writ petition i.e.
CWP-135-2023, with a limited prayer that the witnesses which are common in departmental proceedings and the criminal trial be not examined and this Court on 06.01.2023, after issuing notice of motion has also passed an interim order directing the respondent to carry on the enquiry proceedings without recording the evidence of common witnesses as cited in the criminal trial.

Even the 2 of 5 drill of the procedure prescribed under Regulation 7(A)(1) of the UHBVNL (Punishment &
Appeal) Regulations, 2018, has not been followed.
The punishing authority was obligated to issue a show-cause notice before awarding the punishment as mandated by the aforesaid Regulation.
As such, the disciplinary proceedings conducted by the respondents stand vitiated, rendering the entire process unsustainable in law.

3. Per contra, learned counsel for respondents No.1 to 5, appearing on advance notice, submits that the petitioner was involved in a serious case registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act and he was provided adequate opportunity, however, he could not controvert the fact that the Enquiry Officer was appointed when he was 84 years of age and further the drill of Regulation 7(A)(1) of the UHBVNL (Punishment & Appeal) Regulations, 2018, has not been followed, before passing the punishment order.
4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, it transpires that respondent No.6 was appointed as Enquiry Officer when he was 84 years of age.

This issue was considered by this Court in CWP-27601- 2022, titled as Sukhbir Singh vs State of Haryana and others, wherein it has been observed as under:-
One fails to understand non-compliance of, what is otherwise having very plain and simple meaning, instructions dated 15.03.2022 (Annexure P-10)envisaging, as clear as daylight, that eligibility criteria for empanelment of retired officers as Enquiry Officers must 3 of 5 ensure that the maximum age of Inquiry Officer should not be more than 70 years.

entities.text: Sukhbir Singh vs State of Haryana and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even the renewal of the term of an Inquiry Officer cannot be made beyond the age of 70 years.

Reference may be had to Para (ii) sub-clause (b) and (c) of Clause 1 of eligibility criteria per instructions, ibid.
2.
While issuing the instructions, Chief Secretary office was fully conscious of the fact that there were 14 Inquiry Officers, who were above 70 years of age.
And yet, a conscious call was taken, and Kulwant Singh vs Chairman, Haryana Power Utilities And ... on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12134564/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 rightly so, not to empanel them after attaining the age of 70 years {Clause (c) of (ii)}.

Appointment of respondent No.3 herein, who is stated to be 84 years of age, as Inquiry Officer vide order dated 04.10.2022 vide Annexure P-5, appears to be in gross violation of the crystal clear administrative instructions ibid.
3. Notice of motion.
4. On advance service of copy of the petition, learned State counsel appears and accepts notice on behalf of respondent-State of Haryana and seeks time to get instructions and file return.

5. Adjourned to 08.12.2022.
6.

Meanwhile, let an affidavit of respondent no.1 i.e., Additional Chief Secretary be filed as to how many of the empanelled Inquiry Officers are; (a) more than 70 years of age and; (b) above 70 and total number of enquiries being handled by them before issuance of instructions and; (c) above 70 and number of enquiries assigned to them after issuance of instructions (supra).
7.
On oral request of learned counsel for the petitioner, Chief Secretary of State of Haryana is made as party-respondent No.5. Registry to make necessary correction/addition in the memo of parties.
Chief Secretary 4 of 5 is requested to ensure that his administrative instructions are strictly complied with by all the Administrative Secretaries of Boards/Corporations etc.
His affidavit of compliance be also filed.
8. In the meantime, inquiry proceedings against the petitioner shall remain stayed.
5. In the said case, the order qua appointment of Enquiry Officer was later on withdrawn and the writ petition was disposed of as having been rendered infructuous.

6. In view of the Instructions dated 15.03.2022 (Annexure P- 29) as well as the order passed by this Court on 02.12.2022 in Sukhbir Singh's case (supra), the present petition is allowed and the appointment of Enquiry Officer vide order dated 14.07.2022 (Annexure P-3) along with all subsequent orders including the punishment order dated 23.05.2023 (Annexure P-24) are set-aside, as the same have been passed without following the drill of Regulation 7(A)(1) of the UHBVNL (Punishment & Appeal) Regulations, 2018.

7. However, liberty is granted to the respondents to start the de novo disciplinary proceedings against the petitioner in accordance with the applicable UHBVNL (Punishment & Appeal)
Regulations, 2018 and appoint an Enquiry Officer in terms of the Instructions dated 15.03.2022 (Annexure P-29).

(HARPREET SINGH BRAR)
